text:
**False**

The claim is a longstanding myth. The Great Wall is generally not visible to the naked eye from low Earth orbit (the relevant “space” altitude for human spaceflight, roughly 160–400+ km). Its typical width (a few to ~10 m) falls well below the angular resolution of the unaided human eye at those distances, and its materials/color often blend with the surrounding terrain. Astronaut reports (including from China’s Yang Liwei and various NASA/ISS crew) and NASA assessments confirm it is not discernible without optical aid; photographs that show it use cameras, zoom, or enhanced contrast, not naked-eye viewing. It is entirely invisible from the Moon. 

“From space” is sometimes loosely interpreted, and rare near-ideal lighting/atmospheric conditions have prompted occasional marginal claims, but these do not support the popular statement that the Wall is visible with the naked eye.
